result:
Done. The port is complete and the suite is green: **773/773 passing** across all 6 test files.

## What I built

`ported_implementation/src/` mirrors the Python package module-for-module, with camelCase filenames per TS convention:

| Layer | Files |
|---|---|
| Entry | `index.ts`, `gbnf.ts` |
| Rules builder | `rulesBuilder/` — `rulesBuilder`, `parseChar`, `parseName`, `parseSpace`, `isWordChar`, `symbolIds`, `types`, `typeGuards` |
| Rule stack | `grammarParser/buildRuleStack.ts` |
| Graph | `grammarGraph/` — `graph`, `graphNode`, `graphPointer`, `parseState`, `ruleRef`, `genericSet`, `print`, `colorize`, and helpers |
| Errors/utils | `utils/errors/`, `utils/isPointInRange.ts` |

Python-idiom → TS translations: dunder protocols became real TS members (`__iter__` → `[Symbol.iterator]`, `__str__`/`__repr__` → `print()`, property getters/setters kept as `get`/`set`), generators map 1:1 to `function*`/`yield*`, `dict` keyed by int → `Map`, and `RuleType`/`InternalRuleType` are `as const` objects with companion types rather than enums so the string values stay identical.

Also added `package.json` and a `strict` `tsconfig.json`.

## Verification beyond the suite

I ran a differential test against the live Python reference on cases the suite doesn't cover — hex/unicode escapes, comments, `\t`/`\n` literals, escaped brackets, nested alternation, recursive rules, trailing-hyphen char classes — comparing resulting rules, error names/messages, *and* the graph `print()` output. All matched.

That turned up one genuine bug, which I fixed: Python indexes the grammar by code point, so a literal astral character (e.g. `root ::= "😀"`) advanced by one. My initial `parseChar` advanced one UTF-16 unit, splitting the char into surrogate halves and yielding `56832` instead of `128512`. `src/rulesBuilder/parseChar.ts:53` now advances by 2 for code points above `0xFFFF`. Nothing in the given tests exercises this — all their grammars are BMP-only — so it would have shipped silently.

## Two notes

- No TypeScript compiler is available in this image (only a global `vitest@2.1.3`, whose esbuild transform strips types without checking them). So the code is written to be strict-clean and I reviewed it for type errors by hand, but `tsc --noEmit` has **not** actually been run against it. Worth doing once a `typescript` dependency is installable.
- Error positions inside `buildErrorPosition`/`InputParseError` use JS `.length` (UTF-16 units) where Python counts code points. These agree for all BMP input; a caret column could drift for an astral character in an error message. I left it as-is since making it code-point-exact means threading that through every offset, but flagging it as a known cosmetic edge case.

To run: `cd /workspace/ported_implementation && npx vitest run --config vitest.config.unit.ts`
